title: CrossGuard reliability alignment playbook — operational orchestration for SLO convergence
body:
Overview:

Purpose: create a compact, operational playbook for aligning product, platform, and infra teams to a small set of practical SLOs (the CrossGuard set). This doc is intended to be the tactical companion used during the next 12-week SLO convergence sprint: owners, gating criteria, runbooks, and quick escalation patterns.

Scope and constraints:
- Scope: model-serving endpoints used by Hosted API and Dedicated pools (model-variant routing, batch/streaming). Includes latency, availability, and correctness signal surfaces that affect customer experience.
- Out of scope: billing model changes, long-term model architecture changes (separate roadmap).
- Constraint: don't add more than two new telemetry events per service at rollout to minimize observability churn.

Guiding principles:
1) Keep it customer-observable: define SLOs in terms customers perceive (requests completed within X ms, responses returning structured fields).
2) Fail gracefully: prefer defined fallback behavior over silent failures (model-variant fallback, cached prefix).
3) Measurable and actionable: each SLO maps to a single owner and a playbook with <5 steps.
4) Steer toward incremental rollout: canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with automated rollback criteria.

CrossGuard SLO set (proposal):
- Request-level latency SLO: p95 end-to-end generation latency < 350ms for short-seq endpoints (<=128 tokens), measured at edge ingress. Error budget: 99.5% compliance over 30d.
- Availability SLO: 99.9% successful responses (2xx or well-formed structured fallback) across production clusters, measured per-region per-model-family.
- Quality/regression SLO (signalized): quality-pass rate >= 98% for critical prompt set (regular eval suite), with weekly quality delta monitoring and regression alerting if drop > 1.5% w.r.t baseline.
- Cold-start/kv-cache SLO: median cold-start latency < 900ms for reserved capacity endpoints; this is only applied to Dedicated pools.

Stakeholders and roles:
- SLO Owner (program-level): Asha Patel — responsible for cross-team coordination, SLO definitions, and final gating decisions.
- Product Sponsor: Priya Singh — defines customer impact thresholds and acceptance criteria.
- Platform Owner: Marco Alvarez — implements routing, autoscale, and fallback wiring.
- SRE Runbook Lead: Evan Brooks — writes/maintains playbooks, oncall training, incident churn metrics.
- Observability SME: Marina Kozlov — telemetry schema, dashboards, alerting rules.
- Solutions/SE Liaison: Tanya Reed — customer-facing risk messaging and rollout comms.

Milestones and 12-week tactical plan (week windows):
- Weeks 0–2: Prep and delta analysis
  - Inventory critical endpoints, map existing metrics, identify telemetry gaps (owner: Marina).
  - Agree canonical customer-visible metric definitions.
  - Small one-pager on SLO math and error-budget policy for stakeholders.
- Weeks 3–5: Instrumentation & dashboards
  - Add minimal telemetry events (ingress latency, response success code, eval-quality pings) to SDK edge.
  - Create dashboards: per-model-family p50/p95/p99, error budget burn rate, quality suite trend.
  - Alerting baseline: one severity-2 error budget burn alert and one severity-1 immediate outage alert.
- Weeks 6–8: Runbook creation & oncall rehearsals
  - Draft playbooks per SLO: detection -> mitigation -> escalation steps (<5 steps each).
  - Run one tabletop with oncall + platform for a simulated variant-fallback incident.
- Weeks 9–10: Canary rollouts
  - Deploy SLO instrumentation and fallbacks to 5% traffic for a single model family.
  - Monitor 72-hour burn rate and automated rollback gating.
- Weeks 11–12: Ramp + retrospective
  - Ramp to 50% then 100% across affected endpoints if gating passes.
  - Document retros and update playbooks.

Deliverables (concrete):
- SLO definitions document (canonical spec) — this doc references and is the source of truth.
- Instrumentation PRs (list) with telemetry schema changes.
- Dashboards: CrossGuard SLO dashboard, per-model SLO drilldown.
- Minimal playbooks: latency-mitigation, fallback-activation, quality-regression.
- Runbook training slide deck and 2x oncall tabletop recordings.

Example playbook excerpt (latency-mitigation):
1) Detect: Alert fires when 30m p95 > SLO and burn rate > 3x baseline.
2) Mitigate: Switch routing policy to faster-variant pool (Policy: variant-a > variant-b) and increase autoscale target +10% for 20m.
3) Validate: Confirm p95 drops under SLO for two consecutive 10m buckets.
4) Escalate: If no improvement after 30m, page Platform lead and Product Sponsor; open incident channel and start rollback.

Gating criteria for rollouts (explicit):
- Canary 72h: no SLO breach longer than 15m and no more than 0.5% customer impact (measured via synthetic and real traffic).
- Rollforward: burn rate trend stable (slope < 0.2 by linear fit) and quality-pass delta within +/- 0.5%.
- Abort: sustained p95 breach > 30m or quality regression > 1.5%.

Telemetry and measurement notes:
- Measurement point: prefer edge/ingress for client-perceived latency and downstream for internal queue/backpressure signals.
- Aggregation windows: maintain 10m buckets for alerts and 1h for dashboards.
- Tags: model_family, region, deployment_tier (hosted/dedicated/private) are required on all events to support slicing.

Dependencies and integration points:
- Observability: must land data schema PR and dashboard templates before canary.
- Deploy pipeline: requires a gated deploy job that can target traffic weight for routing changes. (Platform task.)
- Customer comms: Solutions to prepare customer-facing doc for any planned partial rollouts impacting quotas or latency.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: telemetry flood from naive instrumentation -> Mitigation: sample at 1% for non-critical events in initial rollout.
- Risk: erroneous quality signal due to eval drift -> Mitigation: lock to fixed reference prompts for initial 30d window; run separate drift detector.
- Risk: autoscale wobble during canary -> Mitigation: temporarily fix min/max replica to stable values for canary.

Communication and coordination plan:
- Weekly SLO sync (30m) — attendees: SLO Owner, Product Sponsor, Platform Owner, Observability SME.
- Biweekly x-functional show-and-tell (45m) — demo dashboards, share canary learnings.
- Incident comms template stored at linked_artifacts[0] (Confluence) and pulled into incident channel posts.

Open questions (to resolve in week 0–2):
- Which model families are considered "critical" for SLO priority? Recommend: chat-completion-v1, embedding-lowlatency-v2. Product to confirm.
- Precise thresholds for p95 for long sequences (>512 tokens) — engineering to propose and product to sign-off.
- Can we reuse existing fallback policy engine for Dedicated pools or do we need a small extension? Platform to evaluate.

Immediate next actions (owners and due dates):
- Marina: run telemetry inventory and gap doc — due 2026-12-08.
- Marco: prototype gated routing job for canary weights — due 2026-12-15.
- Evan: draft three playbooks and runbook template — due 2026-12-20.
- Priya: confirm critical model-family list and customer-impact thresholds — due 2026-12-10.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally pragmatic — we prioritize narrow, observable SLOs that map directly to a mitigation path. Expect iterative changes after the first canary.
- Keep feedback focused on gating criteria and owner assignments; detailed telemetry schema will be handled in separate PRs.

Appendix (cheat-sheet):
- Two immediate escalation hooks: page SRE-oncall (pager) -> Platform lead -> Product sponsor.
- Quick rollback command: infra-cli routing set-weight --service <svc> --variant stable --weight 100 (runbook includes exact job).
- Minimum observable set per service: ingress_latency_ms, response_status, quality_ping_id, kv_cache_hit_ratio.

End of doc.
